prose.text: Besides the shared enrollment keys, the iOS and Android parameter tables carry keys for their own tunnel, DNS and device checks.

ios-per-app-vpn.statement: For per-app VPN deployments on iOS, newBindFlow enables a multithreaded binding of Client Connector's microservices to its virtual interface (on by default), and PAVConnectionSynced delays the per-app VPN connection until Client Connector is connected (off by default).

quotes: Enables multithreaded implementation of Zscaler Client Connector microservices binding with Zscaler Client Connector virtual interface.
1 = Enable (default) 0 = Disable | Applicable to per-app VPN deployments only.
Delays Per-app VPN connection until Zscaler Client Connector is connected.
1 = Enable 0 = Disable (default)

ios-switches.statement: Other iOS keys, all off by default: SkipInterfaceInstallation shows the VPN icon only while the user is logged in to Client Connector (Tunnel SDK 3.7 or later); DropNonRoutingTraffic drops traffic without routes; MatchDomainsNoSearch stops Private Access match domains being appended as search domains; disableCaptivePortalNotification suppresses notifications when a captive portal is detected.

quotes: When enabled, only shows VPN icon in iOS when user is logged into Zscaler Client Connector.
Requires Tunnel SDK version 3.7 and later.
| DropNonRoutingTraffic | Drops traffic without routes.
When enabled, Private Access match domains are not appended as search domains on the device.
When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector suppresses notifications when it detects a captive portal.
1 = Enable 0 = Disable (default)
1 = Enable 0 = Disable (default)
1 = Enable0= Disable (default)
1 = Enable0= Disable (default)

ios-system-dns.statement: On iOS, SystemDNSEnabled makes Client Connector resolve DNS queries that are not forwarded to the Zscaler cloud with the system DNS, falling back to Google DNS if that fails; 1 enables it and 2, the default, disables it.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector uses this parameter to resolve DNS queries which aren't forwarded to the Zscaler cloud.
If Zscaler Client Connector fails to resolve the DNS using the system DNS domain, it falls back to Google DNS.
1 = Enable2 = Disable (default)

android-custom-dns.statement: On Android, Client Connector uses the device's DNS server by default; customDNS sets another DNS server by IP address.

quotes: By default, Zscaler Client Connector uses the device's DNS server. You can change the value to another DNS server using this setting.

android-rooted-emulator.statement: Client Connector does not run on rooted Android devices or emulators unless allowRunningOnRootedDevice (from 3.7, formerly allowZccOnRootedDevice) or allowRunningOnEmulator (formerly allowZccOnEmulator) is set to 1.

quotes: Restricts users from running Zscaler Client Connector on a rooted device. Enter 1 to allow users to run Zscaler Client Connector on a rooted device.
This parameter was formerly allowZccOnRootedDevice.
Restricts users from running Zscaler Client Connector on an emulator.
This parameter was formerly allowZccOnEmulator.
Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 3.7 and later for Android

android-http-auth-hosts.statement: On Android from 4.2, httpAuthAllowedHosts lists the hosts allowed for HTTP Basic authentication in the SAML WebView and for client certificate requests during SAML authentication; requests from other hosts are cancelled. It is mandatory for those requests, takes FQDNs without scheme or path, rejects wildcards, and a listed domain also matches its subdomains.

quotes: Use this parameter to specify a comma-separated list of hosts allowed for HTTP Basic authentication in the SAML WebView and for client certificate requests during SAML authentication.
allows these requests only from those hosts and cancels all others.
Mandatory parameter for HTTP Basic authentication and clientCert request.
Wildcard (*) character not accepted.
Requires Zscaler Client Connector version 4.2 or later for Android.
